stories.headline: US inflation eases to 3.4% in July, keeping a September Fed hike on the table

key_facts.fact: The US Consumer Price Index rose 0.1% in July on a seasonally adjusted basis, after falling 0.4% in June, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on August 12, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.1 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in July after falling 0.4 percent in June, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today.

key_facts.fact: Over the 12 months to July the all-items index rose 3.4%, down from 3.5% in the year to June — a second consecutive month of deceleration.
key_facts.excerpt: The all items index rose 3.4 percent for the 12 months ending July after rising 3.5 percent for the 12 months ending June.

key_facts.fact: Core CPI, which strips out food and energy, rose 0.2% in the month and 2.5% over the year, easing from 2.6% in June.
key_facts.excerpt: Year-over-year core CPI (which excludes volatile food and energy costs) rose 2.5%, lagging the June rate of 2.6%. ... Core inflation rose 0.2%, matching the June decrease.

key_facts.fact: The energy index was still up 14.7% year over year, with the food index up 3.0%, showing how much of the remaining inflation comes from the Iran war energy shock.
key_facts.excerpt: The energy index increased 14.7 percent for the 12 months ending July. The food index increased 3.0 percent over the last year.

key_facts.fact: Gasoline prices were up 24.6% year on year in July, down from 26.7% in June, as the energy shock from the war with Iran continued to ease.
key_facts.excerpt: Gasoline prices rose 24.6% yoy, down from 26.7% in June, while fuel oil prices increased 39.1%, compared with 42.9% previously.

key_facts.fact: The print landed exactly in line with FactSet consensus, which had looked for 0.1% monthly and 3.4% annual headline CPI and 0.2%/2.5% core.
key_facts.excerpt: Economists had expected CPI to rise 0.1% on a monthly basis and increase 3.4% year over year in July, according to the consensus estimates from FactSet.

key_facts.fact: The Fed has held the federal funds rate at 3.50%-3.75% since its July 29 meeting, in a 9-3 vote in which Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all wanted a quarter-point hike.
key_facts.excerpt: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent ... Voting against the monetary policy action were Beth M. Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie K. Logan, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

sources.title: July CPI Report Shows Inflation at a 3.4% Annual Rate

stories.headline: IEA cuts 2026 oil supply forecast to -4.3 million bpd as Hormuz stays shut

key_facts.fact: In its August 12, 2026 Oil Market Report, the IEA said global oil supply will fall by 4.3 million barrels per day this year — around 4% of world supply — to 102.02 million bpd, its lowest forecast yet for 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Global oil supply will fall by 4.3-million barrels per day, or around 4 per cent, this year, the International Energy Agency said in its monthly oil market report on Wednesday ... will take total supply to the IEA's lowest forecast yet for this year at 102.02-million bpd.

key_facts.fact: That is a downgrade from the 3.7 million bpd decline the agency projected in its July report.
key_facts.excerpt: The expected supply drop compares with the 3.7-million bpd forecast in the IEA's July report.

key_facts.fact: The IEA now sees supply running about 1.27 million bpd below demand for the year, widening from an 860,000 bpd deficit implied by its July numbers, and expects a 1.8 million bpd deficit in the July-September quarter — the deepest quarterly shortfall since 2021.
key_facts.excerpt: That would put global oil supply around 1.27-million barrels per day below demand this year, widening from an 860,000 bpd deficit implied from the IEA's July forecasts. ... The IEA expects an oil market deficit of 1.8-million bpd over July-September.

key_facts.fact: Gulf production rose 2.5 million bpd in July to 23.9 million bpd but remained 8.3 million bpd below pre-war levels, while regional exports fell 2.1 million bpd to 15 million bpd after the strait was effectively closed again in early July.
key_facts.excerpt: Gulf oil production rose by a further 2.5 mb/d in July to 23.9 mb/d, still 8.3 mb/d below pre-war levels. Regional exports, including routes bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, fell by a sharp 2.1 mb/d to 15 mb/d after the key passageway was effectively closed again in early July.

key_facts.fact: The agency also cut its 2026 demand forecast by another 510,000 bpd, now expecting global oil demand to contract by 1.6 million bpd this year.
key_facts.excerpt: World oil demand is forecast to decline by 1.6 mb/d in 2026, 510 kb/d more than our estimate in last month's Report, as the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz and elevated fuel prices continue to weigh on oil consumption.

key_facts.fact: Global oil stocks have already been drawn down by a cumulative 410 million barrels since the Iran war began; the IEA expects a 4.61 million bpd surplus in 2027 only if the conflict de-escalates.
key_facts.excerpt: That surplus could allow oil stocks to recover to their February 2026 level by the middle of next year, the IEA said, after 410-million barrels of cumulative stock draws since the Iran war started.

stories.headline: US Navy helicopter disables cargo ship running Iran blockade as Houthi attack kills six

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said on Tuesday, August 11, that a Navy MH-60 helicopter fired two Hellfire missiles at the Panama-flagged cargo vessel Vela Nova in the Gulf of Oman, targeting its engine room and disabling its steering gear.
key_facts.excerpt: In a statement, US Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees the Middle East, said a Navy helicopter fired two Hellfire missiles at the Panama-flagged Vela Nova cargo vessel. ... The attack targeted the ship's engine room and disabled its steering gear.

key_facts.fact: CENTCOM said the ship had ignored repeated warnings while sailing toward an Iranian port, and that US forces have now disabled 55 commercial vessels under the blockade of Iranian ports, plus three 'non-compliant' vessels, and boarded two.
key_facts.excerpt: CENTCOM said US forces had disabled 55 commercial vessels throughout its blockade on Iranian ports, disabled three "non-compliant vessels", and boarded two.

key_facts.fact: At the southern end of the Red Sea, four crew members were killed in a suspected Houthi attack on the Egyptian-owned cargo vessel Tihamah in the Bab al-Mandeb strait, and two Yemeni rescuers also died — the first deaths from Houthi strikes on shipping since the war on Iran began in late February.
key_facts.excerpt: four crew members were killed in a suspected Houthi attack on a small cargo vessel in the Bab al-Mandeb strait, according to Yemen's Transport Ministry. Two Yemeni rescuers from an anti-Houthi military group were also killed ... The killings on board the Egyptian-owned Tihamah would be the first by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi strikes on shipping since the war on Iran began in late February.

key_facts.fact: Mohsen Rezaei, newly appointed secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told China's ambassador in Tehran that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until Washington ends its military campaign, lifts the naval blockade, releases Iran's frozen assets and agrees to a region-wide ceasefire including Gaza and Lebanon.
key_facts.excerpt: "As long as the US does not change its behaviour and accept Iran's conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will not be reopened," Rezaei told Cong Peiwu ... he insisted on an end to the US's naval blockade on Iranian ports as well as a region-wide ceasefire, including in Gaza and Lebanon.

key_facts.fact: Pakistan's interior minister Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran on Tuesday for talks with President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi as Islamabad joins Qatar and Oman in mediating; Qatar said Iran-Oman talks on Hormuz shipping routes had reached an advanced stage.
key_facts.excerpt: In Tehran, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Pakistan's interior minister ... Qatar – another mediator in the conflict – said talks between Iran and Oman on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz had reached an advanced stage.

key_facts.fact: Trump wrote on Truth Social that the US has 'total control' over the Strait of Hormuz and that its naval blockade is being called 'a wall of steel'.
key_facts.excerpt: "The U.S.A. has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT! Our Naval Blockade is being called, by everyone, 'A WALL OF STEEL,' and there is nothing Iran can do about it," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

key_facts.fact: The war, which began with US and Israeli strikes on February 28, has killed at least 3,527 people in Iran with more than 27,000 wounded, plus at least 18 Americans.
key_facts.excerpt: In Iran, at least 3,527 people have been killed, while more than 27,00 have been wounded. At least 18 Americans have also died.

stories.headline: Researchers disclose first end-to-end autonomous AI agent attack on Taiwan's government

key_facts.fact: Israeli cyberdefence firm Dream published a technical breakdown on Tuesday, August 11, 2026 detailing an attack in which suspected China-linked operators used open-source AI agents to run a near-autonomous intrusion into an Asia-Pacific government's systems; the Financial Times reported the findings on August 12 and a person familiar with the case identified the target as Taiwan.
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli firm Dream Security recovered the workspace and pieced together exactly how the system functioned. Dream Research Labs laid out the details in a technical breakdown published Tuesday. ... The Financial Times first reported the breach hours after Dream's blog appeared, citing the same findings.

key_facts.fact: The campaign ran over four days at the start of July 2026, deploying up to eight AI agents in parallel across 12 attack waves, mapping 21 government systems and switching tactics whenever a route was blocked.
key_facts.excerpt: Over four days at the start of July, the system deployed as many as eight autonomous agents simultaneously, mapping 21 government systems, identifying vulnerabilities and changing tactics when its attempts were blocked.

key_facts.fact: The operation compromised at least 85 government user accounts and extracted more than 2,500 personnel records before expanding into Taiwan's nuclear safety agency and at least seven energy companies.
key_facts.excerpt: The attack compromised at least 85 government user accounts and extracted more than 2,500 personnel records, before expanding to Taiwan's nuclear safety agency and at least seven energy companies, according to Dream's research.

key_facts.fact: The tool was assembled from two publicly available agent frameworks, Hermes and OpenClaw; researchers found the evidence in a 160MB online archive containing 1,395 files.
key_facts.excerpt: Dream researchers identified evidence of the attack in a 160MB online archive containing 1,395 files. The archive showed that the hacking tool used two open-source AI agent systems, Hermes and OpenClaw.

key_facts.fact: Dream could not identify which AI model powered the agents, but said its safeguards were bypassed by framing the intrusion as an authorised penetration test; internal communications were in Simplified Chinese while the stolen data was in Traditional Chinese.
key_facts.excerpt: The researchers could not determine which AI model powered the agents. The data indicated, however, that the model's safeguards had been bypassed by presenting the hacking activity as an authorised exercise intended to test system vulnerabilities. ... the use of Simplified Chinese in internal communications ... indicated a high probability that the operator was connected to China.

key_facts.fact: Taiwan's National Security Bureau reported in January that the island faced an average of 2.6 million China-origin cyberattacks a day in 2025, up 6% on the year before.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwan's National Security Bureau reported in January that the island faced an average of 2.6 million Chinese cyberattacks a day in 2025, a 6 per cent increase from the previous year.

key_facts.fact: Dream was founded in 2023 by Israeli entrepreneur Shalev Hulio, co-founder of NSO Group, and former Austrian chancellor Sebastian Kurz; Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs declined to comment on the specific incident, citing confidentiality.
key_facts.excerpt: Dream was founded in 2023 by Israeli entrepreneur Shalev Hulio and former Austrian chancellor Sebastian Kurz. ... A spokesperson at Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs declined to comment to the paper on the hack, citing confidentiality.

stories.headline: Definium's LSD pill wins a second Phase 3, cutting anxiety scores 5.4 points vs placebo

key_facts.fact: Definium Therapeutics (Nasdaq: DFTX) announced on August 12, 2026 positive topline results from Voyage, its first Phase 3 study of DT120, a single 100 µg oral disintegrating tablet of lysergide (LSD), in adults with generalized anxiety disorder.
key_facts.excerpt: On August 12, 2026, Definium Therapeutics, Inc. (the "Company") issued a press release ... announcing positive topline data from the Company's Phase 3 Voyage study of DT120 ODT for the treatment of generalized anxiety disorder.

key_facts.fact: The trial met its primary endpoint: a 5.4-point placebo-adjusted reduction in the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale at week 12 (p<0.0001, Cohen's d=0.81), from -11.6 on DT120 versus -6.2 on placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: The Least Squares (LS) mean change from baseline in HAM-A total score at Week 12 in participants who received DT120 ODT 100 µg was -11.6 compared with -6.2 for participants who received placebo, an LS mean difference of -5.4 points (p<0.0001), corresponding to a standardized effect size of d=0.81.

key_facts.fact: Voyage enrolled 214 adults aged 18 to 74 across roughly 35 US sites; effects appeared as early as day 2 and were sustained at every post-baseline timepoint.
key_facts.excerpt: The study enrolled 214 participants aged 18 to 74 years across approximately 35 sites in the United States ... Efficacy was rapid, with changes seen as early as Day 2 and sustained at all post-baseline timepoints in Part A.

key_facts.fact: It is the second late-stage win for DT120 this summer, following positive Phase 3 results in major depressive disorder reported in June with an 8.1-point placebo-adjusted improvement over six weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: It's the second late-stage win for the company's lead asset this summer. ... The new data build on MDD results shared earlier this summer that saw an 8.1-point placebo-adjusted change in symptoms over six weeks.

key_facts.fact: Jefferies called it one of the strongest placebo-adjusted efficacy benefits seen in GAD and has forecast at least $1.5 billion in peak sales for the indication; Stifel called the data 'a clean win'.
key_facts.excerpt: with Jefferies writing that the drug has shown "one of the strongest [placebo-adjusted] efficacy benefits" in generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), while Stifel dubbed the data "a clean win." ... Previously, Jefferies forecast at least $1.5 billion peak sales in GAD for DT120.

key_facts.fact: No serious adverse events or suicidality signal were recorded; 92% of participants met discharge criteria within eight hours of dosing, with an average of 6.4 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: No new safety signals were identified, including no suicidality signal or suicidal behavior. ... The average time to meeting EoSC criteria was 6.4 hours for participants receiving DT120 ODT in Part A, with a median of 6.1 hours and 92% of participants meeting the EoSC criteria by hour 8.

key_facts.fact: GAD affects roughly 26 million US adults and the last new FDA-approved treatment for the condition came in 2007; a second Phase 3 (Panorama) reads out in September, with an NDA filing possible in the first half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: GAD affects approximately 26 million U.S. adults ... the last new FDA-approved treatment for this condition was nearly two decades ago ... With our Panorama topline results in GAD expected in September

stories.headline: Bank of America takes up to 49.9% of Reliance's Jio Credit in a $1.9B India lending push

key_facts.fact: Jio Financial Services and Bank of America announced on August 12, 2026 a definitive agreement under which BofA will acquire up to 49.9% of Jio Credit Limited, JFSL's wholly-owned non-bank lending subsidiary.
key_facts.excerpt: Jio Financial Services Limited (JFSL) and Bank of America Corporation (BofA) today announced that they have signed a definitive agreement whereby BofA will acquire up to a total of 49.9% interest as a joint venture partner in JFSL's wholly-owned NBFC (non-bank financial company) lending subsidiary, Jio Credit Limited (JCL).

key_facts.fact: The investment is worth up to ₹18,268 crore, about $1.9 billion, made through a preferential allotment of equity shares and warrants.
key_facts.excerpt: The investment of up to ₹18,268 crore (~$1.9 billion USD), will be made through a preferential allotment of equity shares and warrants.

key_facts.fact: The deal initially gives Bank of America a 26.5% equity interest in Jio Credit, rising to 49.9% if the warrants are exercised.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction initially gives Bank of America a 26.5% equity interest in JCL, which can go up to 49.9% upon exercise of the warrants.

key_facts.fact: The transaction is subject to regulatory and statutory approvals and was announced jointly from Mumbai and New York.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction is subject to regulatory and statutory approvals. MUMBAI, India and NEW YORK, Aug. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/

sources.title: Bank of America Enters into a Joint Venture Agreement with Jio Financial Services Limited to Acquire up to 49.9% in Jio Credit Limited

stories.headline: Asiana shareholders approve Korean Air merger, closing a six-year deal for a top-10 airline

key_facts.fact: Asiana Airlines said on Wednesday, August 12, 2026 that its shareholders approved the merger with Korean Air at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting, by an overwhelming majority.
key_facts.excerpt: Asiana Airlines Inc., the country's second-largest carrier, said Wednesday its shareholders have approved its merger with larger rival Korean Air Co., wrapping up nearly six years of the latter's acquisition process.

key_facts.fact: Korean Air's board of directors also approved the merger later the same day.
key_facts.excerpt: Later in the day, Korean Air's board of directors also approved the merger with Asiana Airlines.

key_facts.fact: Korean Air first announced plans to acquire Asiana in November 2020 in a deal valued at 1.8 trillion won (about $1.6 billion), a move that would create the world's 10th-largest airline by fleet size.
key_facts.excerpt: In November 2020, Korean Air announced plans to acquire Asiana in a deal valued at 1.8 trillion won (US$1.6 billion), a move that would create the world's 10th-largest airline by fleet size.

key_facts.fact: The two carriers signed the merger agreement in May 2026, and the combined entity — to be named Korean Air — is scheduled to launch on December 17, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The two airlines signed a merger agreement in May, and the merged entity, to be named Korean Air, is scheduled to launch on Dec. 17.
